nextSteps.step: Step 1: Create the separate Neon database for apps/dinner (via Vercel)
detail: Go to vercel.com and log in.
In the left sidebar, click Storage.
Click Create Database.
Choose Neon (Postgres).
Name it dinner-db — keep it separate, do not reuse or connect to the existing apps/ops database.
Pick a region close to your users (same region as the ops database is fine).
Click Create. Vercel will show connection details — you don't need to copy anything yet.

nextSteps.step: Step 2: Run the migration SQL in Neon's console to create the tables
detail: In Vercel's Storage tab, click into the dinner-db database you just made.
Click the button/link labeled 'Open in Neon' or 'Neon Console' — this opens Neon's own dashboard.
In the Neon console, click SQL Editor in the left sidebar.
If you see a 'Read-only' toggle near the query box, make sure it's OFF — otherwise the migration will fail.
Open the file apps/dinner/prisma/migrations/20260802120000_init/migration.sql on your computer, select all, and copy it.
Paste it into Neon's SQL Editor query box and click Run (or the equivalent execute button).
Confirm success: in Neon's Tables view (sidebar), you should now see 5 new tables — Account, Session, VerificationToken, User, Household.
If it fails mentioning 'read-only', go back and toggle that off, then run again.

nextSteps.step: Step 3: Create a Resend account and get an API key (Albert confirmed Resend as the email provider for magic-link login)
detail: Go to resend.com and sign up (free tier is fine to start).
Verify your email if asked.
Once logged in, go to API Keys in the left sidebar.
Click Create API Key, name it dinner-app, leave permissions as default.
Copy the key shown — it is only shown once, save it somewhere safe for a minute.

Optional but needed to send to anyone besides yourself: go to Domains > Add Domain, add klaargesukkel.com, and add the DNS records it gives you in GoDaddy (same way as other domain records). Until this is verified, Resend can still email your own Resend account address, which is enough to test login yourself.

nextSteps.step: Step 4: Set up the apps/dinner Vercel project with the database and API key from steps 1-3
detail: In Vercel, check if a project called 'dinner' already exists (from when it was a static site).
If it exists: open it, go to Settings. If not: click Add New > Project, import the Klaargesukkel GitHub repo, and set Root Directory to apps/dinner — Framework Preset should auto-detect as Next.js.
In the project's Settings > Environment Variables, add DATABASE_URL: go back to Storage > dinner-db > Connect, and copy the POOLED connection string (not the direct one).
Add AUTH_SECRET: any long random string works, e.g. Xk9mP2vQ7rN4wL8tY5jH3cF6bA1sD0zE9gK2mR7nV4xW6uT — you never need to remember it.
Add RESEND_API_KEY: paste the key copied from Resend in step 3.
Make sure all three are enabled for the Production environment (Preview/Development too if you want branch deploys to work).
Go to Deployments and trigger a new deployment so it picks up the new env vars.

nextSteps.step: Step 5: Real-browser smoke test of the deployed app — magic-link login, all 5 tabs, the import banner, and cross-device sync
nextSteps.waitingOn: Step 4 (Vercel deploy live with all env vars)
detail: Tell Claude Code once steps 1-4 are done — it will trigger/verify the deploy, do a real magic-link login test, click through all 5 tabs (tonight/tracker/library/shopping/rhythm) to confirm data saves and syncs, and test the 'import this device's data' banner if your browser still has old localStorage data.

nextSteps.step: Decide pricing/access model for other families (free, paid, waitlist) — v1 ships scoped to just Albert syncing his own devices, no invite/multi-user-per-household flow yet

name: EyeSpy
description: Demand-signal research tool — reads compliant sources (Reddit API, search API, Google Places reviews, RSS, open data, podcast) plus weekly manual Facebook Group screenshot capture for a region, tracks recurring themes over time, surfaces trends to feed product ideation.
location: apps/ops (/eyespy, /eyespy/[themeId], /eyespy/capture, /eyespy/sources), this repo — live and pulling real signals from 9 sources: IOL RSS, GroundUp Q&A RSS, GroundUp News RSS, Daily Maverick RSS, CapeTalk consumer podcast, Cape Town Service Requests (ArcGIS), Google Search, Brave Search, plus manual Facebook Group capture. Reddit built but blocked on an account hold (see next steps). Google Places and Google Trends still open.

nextSteps.step: Blocked 2026-08-02: Reddit is showing Albert's account "blocked by network security" on reddit.com/prefs/apps — reproduced across a different browser (Edge) and a different network (phone on mobile data), so it looks like an account-level hold rather than anything fixable on our end. Ticket filed with Reddit. Parked, not urgent — everything else (RSS, ArcGIS, Google, Brave, manual capture) is live without it. lib/ingest/reddit.ts is already built and wired in (client_credentials OAuth, r/CapeTown + r/southafrica search for "Durbanville"), just needs REDDIT_CLIENT_ID/REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET once the account is unblocked
nextSteps.waitingOn: Reddit's account hold clearing (could be hours to a couple days) — no need to keep retrying, it won't speed it up

nextSteps.step: Provide Google Places API key
detail: Go to console.cloud.google.com, select the same project used for Search (or create one).
Go to APIs & Services > Library, search for 'Places API', click Enable.
Go to APIs & Services > Credentials, click Create Credentials > API Key, copy it.
Consider restricting the key to the Places API only under the key's settings, for safety.

nextSteps.step: Apply for Google Trends API (alpha) access — new official API (launched July 2025), free for approved testers, gives quantified search-intent data to cross-check qualitative sources. Not urgent, approval timeline unknown
Provide list of 5–10 Durbanville Facebook groups to track, and who's doing the weekly Wednesday capture session

Wire Places into lib/ingest/ once the API key lands (Search and Reddit are done — Google/Brave Search live 2026-08-02, Reddit built and wired, just blocked on the account hold above), and write a Claude-authored per-period digest (DigestReport) to complement the structured dashboard

nextSteps.step: Set up PayFast merchant account for the pilot operator (confirmed default gateway 2026-07-29 — native Split Payments feature means marketplace mode later doesn't need a gateway migration)
detail: Go to payfast.co.za and sign up for a merchant account (the pilot operator's business details, not Klaargesukkel's, since they're the one receiving booking payments).
Complete PayFast's KYC/verification (business documents, bank account details) — this can take a few days, similar to Meta's process, so start early.
Once approved, go to Settings in the PayFast dashboard and note the Merchant ID, Merchant Key, and (if using it) the Passphrase — these get handed to Claude Code for the payment integration.
If marketplace/multi-operator mode is wanted later, look into PayFast's Split Payments feature in their docs — no separate gateway migration needed per the 2026-07-29 decision.
